prompt:
Add a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown` (and `markdown.markdown`): a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0, that shifts the level of every heading Markdown produces by that many (an `h1` becomes an `h2` with 1), never beyond `h6`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- It applies to hash and underline headings, and to headings from extensions such as `md_in_html`.
- The `toc` extension sees the shifted levels (its tokens and `toc_depth`).
- The command line gets `--heading-offset N`.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: I added a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown`, `markdown.markdown` and the command line (`--heading-offset N`), and all 1143 tests pass (112 skipped). It accepts only a whole number from 0 to 5, so -1, 6, 1.0, True, '1' and None all raise ValueError. A new tree processor runs just before `toc` and moves every h1–h6 in the parsed document down by the offset, capped at h6. That covers hash and underline headings, headings inside `<div markdown="1">`, and extensions' headings. `toc` sees the shifted levels in its tokens and `toc_depth`. Raw HTML that Markdown passes through untouched keeps its levels. One case you might not expect: with `md_in_html`, HTML that it parses into the document is shifted too. That includes `<h1 markdown="1">` and a plain `<h2>` written inside a `markdown="1"` div, while the same `<h2>` at the top level stays as written. Tests, the library and command-line docs, and a changelog entry are included. flake8 isn't installed, so I only checked line lengths.
